# dsh-comfyui-supervisor
**Lazy start / idle-exit lifecycle tools for a local ComfyUI server — as a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) pl
start / idle-exit lifecycle tools for a local ComfyUI server — as a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin.**
The plugin starts nothing at boot. It gives the agent three tools to manage ComfyUI on demand:
| Tool | What it does |
| `comfyui_status` | Is ComfyUI up? Which device? Is this instance managed by us? VRAM / version. |
| `comfyui_start` | Ensure ComfyUI is running: probe → spawn a detached supervisor → wait until read

y. |
| `comfyui_stop` | Stop it and release RAM/VRAM. Only kills instances we started unless `force=
comfyui_stop` | Stop it and release RAM/VRAM. Only kills instances we started unless `force=true`. |
The bundled supervisor (`assets/supervise.cjs`, zero dependencies) keeps the process tree alive whil

e
it is in use and kills it after N idle minutes — no more "leave ComfyUI running all day" or
"remem
ber to start it before generating".
> Unofficial community tool. Not affiliated with ComfyUI, DeepSeek or AMD.
## The problem
Local image plugins for DSH (and for every other harness) assume one of two things:

- **ComfyUI is always on** → 3–4 GB of RAM plus a resident GPU allocation while you are not even
gen

erating, or
- **you start it by hand** → the first `generate_image` call fails, and you have to swit

ch windows,
remember the batch file, wait ~40–60 s, then retry.
Both are bad. This plugin makes the lifecycle explicit and automatic: start on demand, exit when idl
th are bad. This plugin makes the lifecycle explicit and automatic: start on demand, exit when idle.

| `comfyRoot` | `D:\Comf

yUI` | Where `ComfyUI_windows_portable` and `logs/` live |
| `idleTimeoutMinutes` | `30` | Kill Comf

yUI after this much time without generation |
| `startTimeoutSeconds` | `300` | How long `comfyui_st
art` waits for readiness |
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`comfyui_status` reads the state file to tell you **whether the running instance is managed**, and
`
comfyui_stop` refuses to kill an instance it did not start unless you pass `force: true`.
The plugin itself performs **no network request and no process spawn at load time** — DSH cold start
is completely unaffected.
## Verified behaviour
Measured on Windows 11, Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S, ComfyUI 0.44.0:
| Action | Result |

| `comfyui_start` from cold | ready in **~10 s**, device `AMD Radeon(TM) 8060S Graphics` |
| `comfyu

i_status` while running | reports device, free VRAM (~101 GB), ComfyUI version, `managed=true` |
| `

comfyui_stop` | Python tree killed, VRAM released, `running=false` |
| idle timeout (tested with `--

idle-min 1`) | killed at exactly 1 minute, lock/state cleaned |
| `comfyui_stop` when nothing runs |

no-op, `changed=false` |
| All three tools through the real DSH tool interface | `status → start →
status → stop` returned the expected values, no restart needed after install |
## Limitations / roadmap

- Process-tree kill uses `taskkill` (Windows). Linux/macOS branch is a TODO.
- Releasing a "service"

other plugins can inject (so a single plugin manages lifecycle) is planned.
